verdict: Fox's revenue rose 22% to $4.6B and profit rose 57% to $957M as television advertising surged — by segment, Television revenue grew 32% and Cable Network Programming 8%.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.note: Fees channels pay to carry Fox's networks and stations — the steady, subscription-like half of the business.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Advertising — up 47%, powered by the Television segment (sports plus political-cycle demand), where ad revenue rose 60%.

segments.name: Content and other
segments.note: Content licensing and other revenue, including Tubi-related and studio activity.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative costs across the networks and stations.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Depreciation and amortization of equipment and intangibles.

opex.name: Restructuring & other corporate
opex.note: Restructuring, impairment and other corporate matters.

otherDetail: Interest expense, net of $80M, plus $143M of non-operating other expense — mostly mark-to-market and investment-related items below the operating line.
footerNote: Net income in the chart is the total of $957M; $943M was attributable to Fox Corporation stockholders and $14M to noncontrolling interests. Revenue is shown by type (distribution, advertising, content); by segment, Television was $2,713M, Cable Network Programming $1,803M and Corporate & Other $246M, less $191M of eliminations.

takeaways.title: Advertising carried the quarter
takeaways.text: Advertising revenue jumped 47% to $2.08B. In the Television segment, advertising rose 60% — live sports and a heavy political-advertising cycle — taking segment revenue up 32% and segment EBITDA from $399M to $934M.

takeaways.title: Cable networks stayed dependable
takeaways.text: Cable Network Programming (Fox News, FS1 and peers) grew revenue 8% to $1.80B and produced $859M of adjusted EBITDA — a ~48% margin on distribution fees that barely fluctuate.

takeaways.title: Profit per share rose two-thirds
takeaways.text: Net income attributable to stockholders was $943M, or $2.20 a share, versus $1.32 a year ago — helped by the ad surge and by a share count that fell from 455M to 428M on buybacks.
